nra_001: You can recognise it by its trunk forking into two great limbs about seven metres up, each forking again, with a rope tied around it. It stands behind the main hall at Naratsuhiko Shrine.
nra_002: You can recognise it by the second tree growing from its base, reaching toward the neighbouring hall through a hole cut in the roof. It stands beside the Naoraiden, near Kasuga Taisha's inner gate.
nra_003: You can recognise it by its blossoms, red, white, peach, striped and variegated all on the same plant, shedding petal by petal rather than whole. It stands atop over a hundred stone steps at Byakugo-ji.
nra_004: You can recognise it by the bamboo growing up through its hollow trunk and out through the crown. It stands on the bend of the Kasuga Taisha approach, near the Nara National Museum.
nra_005: You can recognise it by its three trunks grown into one dome-shaped crown, inside a ring fence with deer grazing up to it. It stands in the middle of the Tobihino meadow, in Nara Park.
nra_007: You can recognise it by the way it leans out over the pond in front of the shrine gate. It stands beside the approach to Himuro Shrine.
